# Stuart J. Green

> Ocean strategist, institutional adviser and author of The Regenerate Leap.

## Professional practice

Stuart offers two advisory pathways: Ocean Strategy & Advisory and Board & Operating Model Advisory. His work connects marine science, ocean governance, investment and institutional delivery with decisions about organisational strategy, governance and capabilities. Blue-Green Advisors, founded in 2017, is the specialist ocean advisory company. Wider board and operating-model engagements are discussed and scoped directly with Stuart, with contractual arrangements agreed for each engagement.

## Public evidence and its limits

- COAST: Blue-Green Advisors participates in the DAI consortium. This is not personal ownership of programme-wide funding or outcomes. https://www.dai.com/our-work/projects/worldwide-climate-and-ocean-adaptation-and-sustainable-transition-coast
- ADB: Stuart Green is credited as co-lead author of the 2025 Oceans and Coral Reefs in Asia and the Pacific publication. Authorship is not programme implementation. https://www.bluegreenadvisors.com/our-work
- Seafood Task Force: Stuart was appointed Senior Consultant in January 2026. This is a personal appointment, not evidence of a separate BGA contract. https://seafoodtaskforce.global/news-views/seafood-task-force-appoints-seafood-systems-strategist-stuart-green-new-role-jan-26

## Book and method

The Regenerate Leap introduces RAZE, ENRICH and GROW for leadership under irreversible change. Recovery and regeneration are distinguished within this leadership framework, not as absolute scientific definitions. Ecological resilience can include adaptation and transformation; natural systems do not prove an organisational model will succeed.

The Regenerate Leap draws on professional experience, ecological thinking and the author's experience of irreversible personal change. These experiences informed the development of the method; they do not constitute independent scientific validation. The Framework diagnostic is a thirteen-question initial self-report assessment, not an independently validated institutional measurement.
